bug_semantics: HTTP/3 QPACK literal decoding trusts a prefix-integer string length from the compressed field section and, in the non-Huffman branch, allocates `new byte[length]` before confirming that many bytes are present. A few wire bytes can claim a ~1 GiB length, forcing a huge heap allocation and DoS (CWE-770/CWE-789) in `QpackDecoder.decodeHuffmanEncodedLiteral`.
flaw_origin: The unbounded allocation was first written on 2020-11-28 in incubator PR #3 member `abe017c47b0e13994071fee2cc9576d7ea338ec3` as `QpackDecoder.decodeStringLiteral`: it read `length` via `decodePrefixedInteger` and executed `byte[] buf = new byte[length]; in.readBytes(buf);` with no `length <= in.readableBytes()` guard. GitHub squash `8110eccd9637f8c2836e7b1ab0d24d9a8bb15bbd` landed those lines; `0b99840af70cd79b7d0b57d07700589e7ba9ad7b` only renamed the helper to `decodeHuffmanEncodedLiteral` while keeping the same non-Huffman allocation.

The surviving unfixed sink is the non-Huffman branch of QpackDecoder.decodeHuffmanEncodedLiteral (4.2.12.Final lines 394-405).
